rows.text: Kambal charges two life for every noncreature spell an opponent casts and hands that two to you. On its own that is a slow trickle. The deck's job is to make the trickle bigger in both directions: multiply the triggers, wall off combat entirely so nobody can pressure you, and then convert the LIFE YOU GAIN back into life they lose. Once that loop is running, every card the table draws is a card that kills them.

rows.name: Kambal, Consul of Allocation
rows.text: every noncreature spell an opponent casts is two life off them and two onto you. Three mana, and it never stops.

rows.name: Delney, Streetwise Lookout
rows.text: doubles the triggered abilities of your creatures with power 2 or LESS — and Kambal is a 2/3. He is the single biggest upgrade in the deck, and he also doubles Suture Priest, Blood Seeker, Starscape Cleric, Mai and Lotho.

rows.name: Mithril Coat
rows.text: flash, indestructible, attaches itself to a legendary creature on entry. Hold it as insurance for Kambal.

rows.name: Flawless Maneuver
rows.text: free with a commander out, and it saves the whole board.

guide.title: Turning your lifegain into their life loss

rows.text: This is what separates the deck from a pile of small taxes. Every point Kambal gains you is a point they lose.

rows.name: Enduring Tenacity
rows.text: whenever YOU gain life, an opponent loses that much. With Kambal out, every noncreature spell they cast drains four instead of two — and it comes back as an enchantment when it dies.

rows.name: Starscape Cleric
rows.text: every lifegain event costs each opponent one, and it flies and cannot block, so it is pure reach.

rows.name: Suture Priest
rows.text: life for every creature you play and life loss for every creature they play.

rows.name: Blood Seeker
rows.text: the same tax on their creature deployment.

rows.name: Kambal, Profiteering Mayor
rows.text: copies every batch of tokens they make, and drains the table for every batch of tokens YOU make — including the ones he just copied.

rows.name: Aetherflux Reservoir
rows.text: this deck's life total climbs past fifty faster than anyone expects. Fifty life to any target is the cleanest kill in the deck.

guide.title: Taxing every spell and every land

rows.name: Mai, Scornful Striker
rows.text: two more life per noncreature spell, from every player.

rows.name: The Frightful Four
rows.text: their first noncreature spell each turn costs its mana value in life.

rows.name: Liesa, Shroud of Dusk
rows.text: two life per spell from EVERY player, including you. She is worth it because you cast the fewest spells at the table, and her commander tax can be paid in life rather than mana.

rows.name: Polluted Bonds
rows.text: two life for every land an opponent plays. Against fetchlands and ramp decks this is enormous, and it is a drain, so Enduring Tenacity sees it.

rows.name: Lotho, Corrupt Shirriff
rows.text: a Treasure every time anyone casts their second spell each turn.

rows.name: Esper Sentinel
rows.text: taxes their first noncreature spell each turn for a card.

rows.name: Scrawling Crawler
rows.text: forces everyone to draw, and every draw they take costs a life.

rows.name: Fate Unraveler
rows.text: a damage per card they draw.

rows.name: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse
rows.text: two life per card they draw, and two GAINED per card you draw — which Enduring Tenacity converts straight back into their life loss.

rows.name: Gleaming Splendor
rows.text: a Treasure whenever an opponent draws their second card, and it can force draws itself.

rows.name: Smothering Tithe
rows.text: Treasures for the whole table's draws.

rows.name: Bloodchief Ascension
rows.text: three quest counters is trivial when the table is losing two life on every spell. After that, every card that hits any opponent's graveyard drains two more.
Nobody can be allowed to attack you, because the deck's clock is slow and its life total is its resource.

rows.name: Ghostly Prison
rows.text: two per attacker or go somewhere else.

rows.name: Sphere of Safety
rows.text: X per attacker where X is your enchantment count. In this deck that is routinely five or six, which is simply unattackable.

rows.name: Moat
rows.text: creatures without flying cannot attack at all.

rows.name: No Mercy
rows.text: anything that connects with you dies.

rows.name: Revenge of Ravens
rows.text: attacking you costs a life per creature and gains you one — another Enduring Tenacity trigger.

rows.name: Marchesa's Decree
rows.text: the same tax, and it makes you the monarch for the extra card.

rows.name: Dáin, Lord of the Iron Hills
rows.text: another attack tax once you have three artifacts or legends, which is immediate.

rows.name: Authority of the Consuls
rows.text: their creatures enter tapped and you gain a life each time. No haste kills, no surprise blockers.

rows.name: Blind Obedience
rows.text: the same for artifacts and creatures, plus extort on every spell you cast.

rows.name: Righteous Aura
rows.text: a repeatable damage prevention shield for two life a shot.

rows.name: Teferi's Protection
rows.text: the full reset against a combo kill or a wrath.

rows.name: Clever Concealment
rows.text: usually free with convoke, and it phases out your whole enchantment board.

rows.name: Idyllic Tutor
rows.text: this deck is mostly enchantments, so it finds Sphere of Safety, Polluted Bonds, Bloodchief Ascension or Enduring Tenacity as needed.

rows.name: Grim Tutor
rows.text: any card at all.

rows.name: Replenish
rows.text: returns EVERY enchantment from your graveyard to the battlefield. After a wrath or a Cyclonic Rift, this rebuilds the entire lock in one card.

rows.name: The Mind Stone
rows.text: once harnessed it blinks a permanent every end step, resetting an enters trigger for free.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares
rows.text: one mana, exile.

rows.name: Anguished Unmaking
rows.text: instant-speed exile for any nonland permanent.

rows.name: Despark
rows.text: two mana for anything expensive, which is what actually threatens you.

rows.name: Generous Gift
rows.text: the catch-all.

rows.name: Damn
rows.text: a removal spell early or a full wrath late — and your board is enchantments, so the wrath is nearly one-sided.

rows.name: Reprieve
rows.text: not a counterspell, so it works under most stax pieces, and it draws.

rows.name: Mangara, the Diplomat
rows.text: draws when they attack you with two or more creatures and when they cast their second spell each turn. He punishes the two things this deck most wants to discourage.

rows.name: Soul-Guide Lantern
rows.text: graveyard hate that cantrips, and it turns off the reanimator decks this wall cannot race.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep an early wall or an early tax, plus mana. Ghostly Prison on turn three is worth more than Kambal on turn three, because the deck loses to being attacked and never loses to being outdrawn.

rows.name: Kambal, Consul of Allocation
rows.text: he is cheap and recastable, so do not hold him back out of fear. He is also the trigger Delney doubles, so having him on the battlefield when Delney lands matters.
Deploy enchantments before Sphere of Safety, not after. The Sphere counts your enchantments as it resolves and afterwards, so a board of five enchantments makes it unattackable immediately.

rows.name: Enduring Tenacity
rows.text: prioritise it once Kambal is out. It doubles the drain on every trigger in the deck, and because it returns as an enchantment when it dies, removal only half-answers it.
